name: Govetts Leap & Cliff Top Track
blurb: Sheer cliffs and a 180 m waterfall, then a clifftop track to Evans Lookout.
weatherNote: Cloud can fill the Grose Valley and hide the view. Skip it in rain: the track follows the cliff edge. The heath has little shade on hot days.
gettingThere: Blue Mountains Line from Central to Blackheath (about 2 hrs 15), then walk 3 km along Govetts Leap Rd to the lookout. Bus 698 goes nearby but runs only a few times a day.
newcomerTip: Drop into the Blue Mountains Heritage Centre on the way for maps and track advice. Our tip: walk from Govetts Leap to Evans Lookout so the big view comes first and you finish at a picnic area.

legs.title: Blue Mountains Line to Blackheath
legs.detail: One or two an hour on weekends (about 2 hr 15)

legs.title: Along Govetts Leap Rd to the lookout
legs.detail: ≈ 3 km, past the Heritage Centre. Bus 698 runs only a few times a day

back.text: It's one way. From Evans Lookout, walk out along Evans Lookout Rd and over the highway to Blackheath station (≈ 5 km, about 1 hr), or walk the track back to Govetts Leap. Trains to Central run about hourly: check the last one.

notes: There's a car park at Govetts Leap lookout with 2 accessible spaces. It's busy on weekends; the Heritage Centre car park is 500 m away (NSW National Parks).
It's one way: from Evans Lookout, walk the track back to your car (≈ 3 km).

routes.ride: Not practical: it's a long, expensive ride. The train is the easy option.

visit.bestTime: Catch a train by about 8:30am so you're on the track by late morning. NSW National Parks says the track is a good winter warm-up, with sun from the east.
visit.hours: The lookouts and track are always open, but can close in bad weather or high fire danger. Blue Mountains Heritage Centre: 9am to 4pm daily, closed Christmas Day.
facilities: Flush toilets and picnic tables at Govetts Leap; toilets and picnic facilities at Evans Lookout
Drinking water at the Blue Mountains Heritage Centre
Cafés in Blackheath village, near the station
visit.access: Govetts Leap lookout is fully accessible: step-free concrete paths from the car park, accessible toilets, seats and 2 accessible parking spaces. Evans Lookout has an accessible path. The Cliff Top track has short steep hills and many steps.
safety: Stay on the track and behind the lookout railings: the track follows the cliff edge
Phone reception is limited. Fill in the free trip intention form and download the Emergency Plus app
A park fire ban runs until 31 March 2027: no wood or solid-fuel fires or stoves
Check NSW National Parks alerts before you go

notice.text: Govetts Leap descent and parts of Rodriguez Pass, which start at the lookout, are closed after rockfalls and landslides. The Cliff Top track to Evans Lookout isn't listed as closed.
